verdict: Leads dropped sharply this week while Google spend rose — action underway.
narrative: In the last 28 days, you received 23 leads at an average cost per lead of $160.25 — but that average is being pulled up by a significant imbalance: Meta delivered all 23 tracked leads at roughly $47 each, while Google Ads consumed $2,601 of your $3,685 total spend and is not showing confirmed lead conversions in the same way. Week-over-week, leads fell 64% while spend rose 28%, which is the core problem this period. We are auditing the top Google campaign immediately to determine whether it is producing qualified contacts or absorbing budget without converting. Separately, 101 leads have entered your pipeline this period with zero signed cases recorded, which points to an intake process gap — not an advertising failure — and we are addressing that with you directly. You should expect tighter Google spend controls and a clearer intake review heading into the next period.

highlights.phrase: leads received in the last 28 days, all attributed to Meta
blended cost per lead this period, up sharply week-over-week due to Google spend with unconfirmed conversions
pipeline opportunities created this period, with follow-through being reviewed

watch_item.issue: Google Ads is consuming 71% of total spend while tracked lead output remains unconfirmed, driving cost per lead to an unsustainable level this week.
watch_item.fix: The top-spending Google campaign is being audited now; budget will be reallocated toward what is converting until performance is confirmed.
